research.summary:
As of 2026-11-18 the US is in a new Fed tightening cycle under Chair Kevin Warsh, who has led the Fed since May 22, 2026. Powell's term as chair ended in May, but he remains a governor.

**Policy so far:**
- Sep 16: the FOMC raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, 12-0. This was the first hike since 2023.
- Oct 28: it held at 3.75-4.00% by 10-2. Cook and Hammack dissented in favor of another hike.

**Market pricing:**
- Futures give about 96% odds of a 25bp hike on Dec 9 and about 4% odds of 50bp.
- More hikes are priced into 2027 (January, April, and about four by Sep 2027).
- That is more hawkish than the September median dots: 4.1% at end-2026 and 4.1% at end-2027.

**Why the Fed is hiking:**
- An energy shock from the US-Iran war, which began in late February 2026, on top of core inflation that is broad and hard to bring down:
  - September CPI was 3.7% y/y.
  - October core CPI rose 0.3% m/m for a third month. There is no official October y/y figure because of the 2025 shutdown data gap.
  - September core PCE was 3.1%, measured after a BEA methodology change that lowered it.
  - October PPI was 6.5% y/y.
- The economy is strong: Q3 GDP grew 3.4%, October payrolls rose 165k and unemployment is 4.1%.

**Why the 10-year is at 5.1-5.3%:**
- The 10-year peaked around 5.33% intraday on Oct 1, the highest since 2002. It is about 5.1% now.
- The rise is mostly higher real yields, not higher inflation expectations. The 10-year TIPS real yield is about 2.87%, roughly an 18-year high; the breakeven is only about 2.26%.
- Contributing causes:
  - The hiking path.
  - A higher term premium tied to deficits (about $40tn of debt and about $2tn a year of deficits).
  - Heavy Treasury supply plus AI-linked corporate bond supply and hedging.
  - Mortgage-hedging flows.
  - A global long-end selloff.
- Treasury's larger buybacks did not cap yields, and all three November refunding auctions tailed. No outright market breakdown has been reported.

**Treasuries as a hedge:**
- In this inflation- and Fed-driven regime they have repeatedly failed to hedge equity drawdowns; mid-November AI-stock turmoil came with rising yields.
- Short flight-to-safety rallies still happen, such as the 10-year at 4.83% on Nov 5.

**Fed independence risk:**
- Trump attacks the 'board' but spares Warsh.
- A White House hearing on removing Governor Cook is set for Dec 14. She refuses to attend unless the panel and procedures change.

**Warsh's changes to how the Fed operates:**
- No dots and no forward guidance.
- From 2027 one meeting a year will be strategy-only, with no rate vote.
- A Balance Sheet Task Force reports in early 2027.

**Oil and the midterms:**
- Brent fell sharply in early November to about $96. That may ease headline inflation, but the Fed is focused on core.
- Democrats won both chambers on Nov 3. Analysts expect little change to Fed policy or the deficit path.

**Upcoming dates:**
- Oct-meeting minutes (Nov 18, 2pm ET; not yet published when checked).
- October PCE (Nov 25).
- FOMC with new projections (Dec 8-9).
- November CPI (Dec 10, after the decision).
- Cook hearing (Dec 14).

The web-search budget ran out near the end, so a few items could not be cross-checked; they are listed under unknowns.

findings.claim:
FACT: The Fed has resumed tightening.
- 2026-09-16: the FOMC raised the fed funds target range 25bp to 3.75%-4.00% by a 12-0 vote, the first hike since 2023 [https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm, 2026-09-16].
- 2026-10-28: it held at 3.75%-4.00% by 10-2. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of another 25bp hike.
- The October statement upgraded activity to 'expanding at a strong pace', said 'Inflation remains elevated' and said 'The Committee will deliver price stability'.
- Interest on reserve balances was kept at 3.90% (per implementation-note coverage).
- The July 2026 hold had three dissents in favor of hikes [AP via ADN, 2026-09-16: https://www.adn.com/business-economy/2026/09/16/federal-reserve-hikes-key-rate-for-1st-time-in-3-years-defying-trump-demands-for-a-cut/].
- The next FOMC meeting is Dec 8-9, with new projections. The November CPI is released Dec 10, the day after the decision [BLS, 2026-11-10].
findings.relevance: Short rates are now rising, the opposite of the 2024-25 easing backdrop. This raises the financing cost built into leveraged ETFs, which tracks short rates, and lifts the yield on cash/T-bills as the risk-off alternative.

findings.claim:
FACT (market pricing from secondary sources; no primary CME data was pulled):
- As of 2026-11-18, futures implied about 96% odds of a 25bp hike on Dec 9 and about 4% odds of 50bp.
- Markets also price hikes in January and April 2027, and about four quarter-point hikes by September 2027 [Trading Economics, 2026-11-17/18]. The source's wording is ambiguous on whether December is counted in the four.
- Right after the October CPI on 2026-11-10, CME FedWatch showed about 100% odds of a December hike (89% for 25bp, 11% for 50bp) [MPA Mag, 2026-11-10: https://www.mpamag.com/us/mortgage-industry/industry-trends/fed-rate-hike-odds-hit-100-as-waller-floats-bigger-december-move/596880].
- Reuters, via StockAnalysis on 2026-11-13, said markets expect a December hike and another in January [https://stockanalysis.com/news/fed-williams-more-rate-hikes-likely/].
- The 2-year yield was about 4.81% on Nov 18. On Nov 10 it jumped 17bp to 4.73%, the largest one-day rise since April 2025. Its 2026 high was 4.92% on Sep 28 [24/7 Wall St, 2026-11-11: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/11/the-2-year-treasury-yield-just-had-its-biggest-jump-in-19-months/].
- The curve still slopes upward: 2s10s is about +28bp (derived from 10y ~5.09% minus 2y ~4.81%).
findings.relevance: Markets expect tightening to continue into mid-2027, more than the Fed's own September median (F3). Both a dovish surprise and further hawkish repricing are live sources of rate volatility, front-end pressure and dollar strength.

findings.claim:
FACT: Medians from the September 16 Summary of Economic Projections. Eighteen participants submitted projections; Chair Warsh submitted no dot.
- Fed funds rate: 4.1% at end-2026, implying one more 25bp hike (June median 3.8%); 4.1% at end-2027 (June 3.6%); 3.9% in 2028; 3.6% in 2029; 3.2% longer run (June 3.1%).
- PCE inflation: 3.7% in 2026 and 2.3% in 2027.
- Core PCE: 3.4% in 2026 and 2.5% in 2027.
- Unemployment: 4.1%.
- GDP: 2.3% in 2026 and 2.4% in 2027.
- Reuters reported that 16 of 18 participants projected at least one more hike in 2026 [https://wmbdradio.com/2026/09/16/fed-forecasts-see-latest-hike-followed-by-another-before-end-of-year/, 2026-09-16].
findings.relevance: The Fed's own path is one more hike, then hold through 2027; markets price more (F2). The December projections will show which side gives way. A rising longer-run rate estimate supports structurally higher yields.

findings.claim:
FACT: Inflation has re-accelerated and is broadening. It was first driven by the energy shock from the US-Iran war, which began in late February 2026.
- September CPI (released 2026-10-14): +0.6% m/m and 3.7% y/y (August 3.4%). Core +0.3% m/m and 2.6% y/y. Gasoline +9.1% m/m [AP via ADN: https://www.adn.com/business-economy/2026/10/14/inflation-worsened-last-month-to-37-in-sign-that-prices-remain-elevated-as-midterm-elections-near/].
- October CPI (BLS, 2026-11-10): headline +0.4% m/m vs 0.3% expected; core +0.3% m/m, the third straight 0.3%; energy +0.7% after +5.2%; shelter +0.3%.
- BLS could not publish 12-month changes for October because October 2025 data were never collected during the shutdown. Gasoline is +37.4% y/y.
- Economists' interpolations put October y/y near 3.8-3.9% headline and about 2.7% core. These are estimates, not official figures [PandaForecast, 2026-11-10].
- September PCE (BEA, 2026-10-29): 3.6% y/y (+0.5% m/m); core 3.1% y/y (+0.3% m/m) [https://www.bea.gov/data/personal-consumption-expenditures-price-index]. This follows the BEA's Sept 30 methodology revision, which cut measured core PCE by about 0.3pp [24/7 Wall St, 2026-10-02].
- October PPI final demand: +6.5% y/y, the highest since November 2022 [investinglive, 2026-11-13].
- University of Michigan year-ahead inflation expectations eased to 4.3% in the November preliminary reading, from 4.7% [2026-11-06].
- Governor Waller (2026-11-10): more than 70% of core PCE services components are above 3% y/y.
findings.relevance: Core inflation running about 0.3% a month (roughly 3.6% annualized) keeps the Fed hiking even as oil falls. October PCE (Nov 25) and November CPI (Dec 10) are the next big catalysts for rate volatility.

findings.claim:
FACT/ANALYSIS: Why the 10-year rose to 5.1-5.3%.

The path:
- About 4% before the war in late February.
- Above 5% in mid-September, the highest since 2007 [Fortune, 2026-09-19].
- About 5.33% intraday on Oct 1, the highest since early 2002; 30-year about 5.67% [Trading Economics, 2026-10-01]. Close of 5.28% on Oct 2 [24/7 Wall St, 2026-10-03].

It has mostly been a real-yield move, not a rise in inflation expectations:
- On Nov 13: 10-year 5.14%, 10-year TIPS real yield 2.87% (around an 18-year high), breakeven only 2.26%.
- Fed staff, in the September FOMC minutes released 2026-10-07, said real rates drove most of the rise in longer yields [https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20260916.htm].
- The minutes cited a higher expected policy path, strong data, geopolitics, uncertainty about Treasury buybacks and heavy AI-related private debt issuance. Market commentary linked these to higher term premiums.

Other drivers cited:
- Fiscal: debt about $40tn, deficits about $2tn a year. The CBO's February 2026 assumption of a 4.1% 10-year for 2026 has already been blown through [Fortune, 2026-09-19].
- Hedging flows: buyers of long AI hyperscaler bonds hedge by selling Treasury futures, and mortgage investors' hedging adds selling pressure. Reuters said the 10s30s spread widening increasingly reflects term premium [Reuters via ARY, 2026-10-09].
- A global long-end selloff: UK 10-year 5.38% and Bund 3.60% on Sep 24 [Bloomberg via swissinfo]; Japan's 10-year at its highest since 1996 [24/7 Wall St, 2026-10-03].

CONTESTED: model decompositions disagree on how much is term premium versus the expected Fed path. One secondary source put the NY Fed ACM 10-year term premium at about 0.73% on Oct 20; this was not verified against the NY Fed.
findings.relevance: High real yields tighten financial conditions and raise the discount rate on long-duration growth stocks (NDX). Inference: high real yields plus a firmer dollar are also a headwind for gold, which fits GLD's drawdown.

findings.claim:
FACT: Treasuries have been an unreliable equity hedge in this inflation- and hiking-driven regime.
- In the week to Nov 13, the combined 2-year jump on Tuesday and Thursday was the biggest since March 2023, and the 10-year's weekly rise was the largest since April 2025. Nvidia/AI turmoil rattled stocks 'without restoring Treasuries' haven role' [Bloomberg-sourced, The Edge, 2026-11-13].
- Trading Economics (2026-11-18) said Treasuries failed to attract safe-haven demand during AI-infrastructure stock weakness, as some funds sold bonds to raise cash.
- By contrast, a brief flight-to-safety rally took the 10-year to 4.83% on Nov 5 during an equity selloff after the midterms [Trading Economics, 2026-11-05: https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield/news/598729].
- Chair Warsh (2026-10-28) said markets showed 'bouts of volatility and shifting correlations'.
- Task-provided data: TLT -2.9% and IEF -1.5% versus QQQ -3.9% from Jul 24 to Nov 17.
findings.relevance: This bears directly on the treasuries risk-off leg. Inference, not a trade call: when the shock is inflation- or Fed-driven, duration and equities can fall together, as in 2022. When it is a growth or sentiment scare, Treasuries can still rally. T-bills yield about 4.1% with no duration risk.

findings.claim:
FACT: Treasury supply is being absorbed, but with visible strain.

November refunding (statement 2026-11-04):
- $125bn in total: 3-year $58bn, 10-year $42bn, 30-year $25bn.
- Treasury 'anticipates maintaining nominal coupon and FRN auction sizes for the next several quarters'.
- Bill auction sizes rise in January.
- Buyback capacity: up to $70bn for liquidity support plus $25bn for cash management.

All three refunding auctions were soft:
- 3-year: tailed about 0.5bp.
- 10-year (Nov 10): 5.020% versus 5.010% when-issued, a 1bp tail. Bid-to-cover 2.46 versus 2.77 at the prior auction; dealers took a larger share [Newsquawk/investinglive, 2026-11-10].
- 30-year (Nov 12): 5.441%, about a 0.4bp tail. Bid-to-cover 2.36 versus 2.54 prior and a 2.45 ten-auction average. The October 30-year had cleared at 5.618% [RTTNews, 2026-11-12: https://www.rttnews.com/3714054/thirty-year-bond-auction-attracts-below-average-demand.aspx].

Buybacks:
- Treasury raised the long-end buyback maximum from $2bn to at least $4bn per operation for Sep 9-Nov 4 [https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0607, 2026-08-19].
- Bloomberg (2026-09-24) said the expanded buyback 'failed to live up to expectations'.

Stress gauges:
- The cost of insuring against a 200bp rise in 10-year swap rates hit its highest since the March 2023 banking crisis [Reuters, 2026-10-09].
- No outright dysfunction has been reported. In the September minutes, a few Fed participants said Treasury markets had been functioning smoothly while stressing planning for possible stress.
findings.relevance: Weak long-end demand plus heavy supply is a channel for term-premium spikes that hit stocks and bonds at once. Auction tails and the February 2027 refunding are the gauges to watch.

findings.claim:
FACT: Fed leadership and the independence fight.
- Kevin Warsh became chair on May 22, 2026. The Senate confirmed him 54-45 on May 13 [NPR Illinois, 2026-05-13: https://www.nprillinois.org/2026-05-13/senate-confirms-kevin-warsh-as-next-chair-of-the-federal-reserve]. Powell's chair term ended in mid-May; he can stay a governor until January 2028.
- After the September hike, Trump called the board 'very hostile' and 'a bunch of politicians' [AP, 2026-09-16].
- On Oct 7 Trump said Warsh is 'one vote' on a Board that 'would like to see the country do badly'. A reporter quoted this at the Oct 28 press conference; Warsh declined to respond and said politics played no role.
- Cook case: the Supreme Court ruled 5-4 on 2026-06-29 (Trump v. Cook) that she can stay while litigation continues, but Trump may try again with notice and a hearing.
- Trump set up a three-member 'committee of inquiry' that includes NEC Director Kevin Hassett. The committee cannot fire Cook; Trump decides [CNBC, 2026-10-09].
- The hearing moved from Nov 5 to Dec 14. On Nov 16-17, Cook's lawyer said she will not participate unless the panel's membership and procedures change.
- A Justice Department probe of Powell ended without charges in late September [CNBC, 2026-10-09].
findings.relevance: Inference: if Trump moves to remove Cook, a hawkish dissenter, after the Dec 8-9 meeting, that would be an independence shock. It could lift inflation-risk premia and term premium and weigh on long bonds and the dollar. This is a tail risk, not the base case.

findings.claim:
FACT: Warsh is changing how the Fed signals and operates.
- He submits no SEP dot. He said: 'I don't believe in forward guidance, absent exigent circumstances', and he will not prejudge meetings.
- From 2027, one of the eight FOMC meetings will be strategy-only, with no rate vote or statement; two will be in 2028.
- A Balance Sheet Task Force will send recommendations to the FOMC 'probably early in the first quarter' of 2027. Warsh has long favored a smaller balance sheet.
- The New York Fed's trading desk paused its reserve-management Treasury-bill purchases (September minutes) [Reuters on the meeting changes, 2026-10-28: https://kfgo.com/2026/10/28/feds-warsh-announces-changes-in-how-future-fomc-meetings-will-go/].
findings.relevance: Less forward guidance means more surprise risk at each meeting. Inference: any decision to shrink the balance sheet further would push more long-duration bonds onto the market, an upside risk to term premium.

findings.claim:
FACT: Fed officials have sounded broadly hawkish since the October meeting.
- Governor Waller (London speech, 2026-11-10): favors a 25bp December hike even if inflation improves. A 50bp hike 'should be considered' if core inflation runs around 0.3% or more, and October core CPI printed 0.3%. He said 'Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk' and cited Fed research suggesting energy shocks pass more into core, possibly into 2027.
- NY Fed President Williams (2026-11-12): 'inflation is persistent' and 'We still have work to do' [StockAnalysis/Reuters, 2026-11-13].
- Dallas Fed President Logan (October 2026): rates need to rise '50 bps or more' [NST/Reuters].
- Cleveland Fed President Hammack favors gradual hikes.
- St. Louis Fed President Musalem says more hikes are needed. Trading Economics reported he said 'as many as four' on Nov 17; this was not independently confirmed.
findings.relevance: The debate is about pace (25bp or 50bp, and how many), not direction. A 50bp December move is a live tail risk.

findings.claim:
FACT: The energy shock is easing but not resolved.
- Brent fell about 16% in the week to Nov 6, its steepest weekly drop since early Covid, after Trump played down new strikes on Iran.
- Brent settled at $92.57 on Nov 9 [NST/Reuters, 2026-11-10] and $95.84 on Nov 13, with WTI at $88.56.
- For comparison, Brent was about $107 on Sep 24, and WTI was just above $100 (+78% YTD) on Oct 28.
- Drivers of the drop: the IEA flagging a growing surplus and rising US inventories.
- Risks remain: the war is in its ninth month, the US blockade of Iran continues, Houthis attacked Saudi sites, and tankers were reported hit near Hormuz.
- Waller (2026-11-10) estimates Hormuz shipping and insurance costs add $20-30 a barrel.
findings.relevance: Lower oil should cool headline CPI in coming months, but the Fed is now focused on core. A re-escalation would revive the oil-to-market-yields link Warsh described on Oct 28.

findings.claim:
FACT: The real economy is strong, which gives the Fed room to hike.
- Q3 GDP advance estimate: +3.4% annualized [Fox Business, 2026-10-29].
- October payrolls: +165k versus about 60-65k expected. August and September were revised up by 84k combined.
- Unemployment: 4.1%.
- Average hourly earnings: +3.1% y/y, below the 3.7% CPI, so real wages are falling.
- Initial jobless claims were at their lowest in 57 years in early November [Trading Economics, 2026-11-05].
- Warsh (2026-10-28): capital spending is at a historically high share of GDP and broadening beyond AI.
findings.relevance: There is no growth scare to support bonds. Strong data plus sticky core inflation means hikes, a headwind for long-duration equities and for Treasuries as a hedge.

findings.claim:
FACT plus labelled OPINION: midterms and fiscal outlook.
- FACT: Democrats won both chambers in the Nov 3 midterms, per AP calls.
- FACT: The 10-year fell to 4.93% on Nov 4 and 4.83% on Nov 5, on lower odds of new tax cuts and spending and on AI-regulation worries. It rebounded to about 5.12% by Nov 13 after the hot CPI and hawkish Fed comments.
- FACT: Treasury's borrowing estimate for the October-December quarter is $618bn.
- OPINION (WisdomTree, 2026-11-11): the midterms will have little effect on Fed policy. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act already sets fiscal policy for about two years, deficits could still widen, larger coupon auctions are 'a matter of timing', and the 10-year should trade in a 4.50-5.25% range [https://www.wisdomtree.com/us/insights/blog/what-do-the-midterm-results-mean-for-rates].
findings.relevance: Divided government lowers the odds of new fiscal stimulus but does not reverse the deficit and supply trend behind the term premium.

findings.claim:
OPINION/FORECAST: views on yields and the Fed path diverge widely.
- Goldman Sachs: 10-year falls to 4.6% in 2027. Goldman also added a March 2027 hike, for a 4.25-4.50% peak [24/7 Wall St, 2026-11-11].
- Brandywine: next 10-year target 5.5%.
- K2 Asset Management: buying 10-year Treasuries around 5.3%.
- Schroders: US rates may need to rise further.
- WisdomTree: 4.50-5.25% range.
- Continuum Economics (2026-09-15): the selloff looked stretched, with a near-term bias toward corrective bounces, but a longer-run upside risk to the neutral real rate and to global fiscal supply.
- Edward Jones (2026-10-29): a December hike, possibly one more in 2027.
- Fed staff (September minutes): headline inflation falls near term as gasoline eases, but reaches 2% only in 2029.
findings.relevance: There is no consensus that yields have peaked. Forecasts span roughly 4.5% to 5.5% on the 10-year, so the bond leg's behavior in the next drawdown is highly uncertain.

unknowns: Minutes of the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting are due 2026-11-18 at 2pm ET but were not yet published when checked; the Fed URL returned 404.
There is no official y/y CPI for October 2026 because BLS never collected October 2025 data. Only economists' interpolations exist (about 3.8-3.9% headline, about 2.7% core).
October PCE (due Nov 25) and November CPI (due Dec 10, after the Dec 9 decision) are not yet known.
The exact futures curve beyond December rests on secondary sources only; no primary CME FedWatch pull was made. It is ambiguous whether 'about four hikes by Sep 2027' includes December.

Not independently confirmed (the web-search budget ran out): Musalem's reported 'as many as four hikes' (Nov 17), and a headline saying Treasury Secretary Bessent urged the Fed not to hike 'too much'.
Not verified: a second-hand report (24/7 Wall St citing Goldman's Mike Mitchell) that Warsh suggested after the July meeting that higher long yields could substitute for rate hikes.

The latest NY Fed ACM term-premium reading is not confirmed; only an Oct 20 figure of about 0.73% from a secondary source was found. Models disagree on how much of the 10-year rise is term premium versus the expected Fed path; a San Francisco Fed-based view cited in a LinkedIn post says term premium contributed nothing since late July.
Unknown: whether the Dec 14 White House hearing on Governor Cook goes ahead without her, whether Trump then tries to remove her, and how courts would respond.
Unknown: what the Fed's Balance Sheet Task Force will recommend in early 2027, and whether the Fed will resume shrinking its holdings.
Foreign demand for Treasuries (official TIC data) for Sep-Nov 2026 was not checked. China's holdings of about $651bn (spring 2026) come only from a secondary source.
Unknown: how the US-Iran war and Strait of Hormuz develop, and the durability of the November oil decline.
The University of Michigan's November long-run (5-10 year) inflation expectations figure was not found.
Debt-ceiling timing and an updated CBO deficit outlook for FY2027 were not verified.

Confirmed:

- BEA (Oct 29): September PCE +0.5% m/m, 3.6% y/y; core +0.3% m/m, 3.1% y/y.
- BLS PPI (Nov 13): final demand +6.5% y/y, the 'largest 12-month rise since ... November 2022' (7.4%).

research.summary: The Nasdaq-100's ~13.5% fall from its Oct 6 record is mostly a de-rating of AI-linked mega-caps and chip stocks. It is not an earnings recession. Two shock legs did most of the damage. First, a chip and AI-capex-financing rout in the week to Oct 16: NDX -5.5%, with the 10-year yield at its highest since 2002, oil above $100 and hot inflation. Second, a post-midterm crash on Nov 5: NDX -6.3%, SOX -12%, after Democrats won both chambers of Congress. Three other things added to it: Alphabet and Meta posting negative free cash flow as capex surged; Nvidia's CEO resigning in a scandal on Nov 12; and tighter AI-chip export rules on Nov 16. Fundamentals stayed strong. S&P 500 Q3 EPS rose 31.9% (IT +69%, semis +133%). On Nov 17 Nvidia beat estimates and guided to $130B; the stock rose ~4% after hours. NDX forward P/E fell to ~19x by Nov 3, its lowest since Oct 2022, and its premium to the S&P 500 was the smallest since 2017. LSEG data show S&P 500 tech trading below the market's forward multiple for the first time since 2017. The key unresolved risk is that 2026-27 earnings depend heavily on hyperscaler capex. Goldman (forecast) estimates AI lifted S&P 500 EPS ~25% above trend and expects capex to become an earnings drag by 2028. Consensus S&P 500 EPS growth for Q2 2027 is only +3%. Institutions have cut risk: the BofA survey shows the biggest tech cut since 2006, and hedge-fund leverage is down. But positioning is not washed out. Survey cash is only 3.6%, semiconductors are still the most crowded trade, and retail kept adding to TQQQ and SOXL. Near-term catalysts: Anthropic's ~$1.4T IPO (pricing Nov 18, trading Nov 19); the Dec 8-9 FOMC, where markets price an ~85-90% chance of a rate hike; and AI-credit and hyperscaler-capex signals.

findings.claim: FACT: The October leg of the decline was led by chips and AI. The Nasdaq-100 fell ~5.5% in the week ending Oct 16, 2026, its worst week since the week ending Apr 4, 2025. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF fell ~10% that week. Reported drivers: worries about how much tech firms are borrowing to fund AI capex, hotter-than-expected inflation, and oil above $100/bbl. ANALYSIS BY THE ARTICLE'S AUTHOR (QQQ back-test): since 2010, QQQ was higher a year later after 25 of 26 weeks with drops of 4% or more. In 2000-02 it was higher after 0 of 18 such weeks. Bloomberg reported the NDX closed in correction on Nov 2: -1.4% to 27,989.82, more than 10% below the Oct 6 peak, still +11% YTD, and its third correction of 2026 (Bloomberg, 2026-11-02, https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-02/nasdaq-100-enters-correction-as-megacap-results-amplify-ai-fears; paywalled, seen only via the search excerpt).
findings.relevance: This is the backdrop to the ~Oct 16 break below the 100-day EMA: a chip and AI-capex-financing shock on top of an inflation, oil and rates shock. Since 2010 the base rate favours recovery within 12 months. The 2000-02 capex bust is the case where that base rate failed, and it is the analog investors are now debating.

findings.claim: FACT (data from a Citadel Securities note; its constructive tone is OPINION): Scott Rubner's Global Market Intelligence note 'November: The Setup Improves' (Nov 4, 2026; data to Nov 3; Bloomberg/S&P Global) said: the Nasdaq-100 traded at 19.1x forward earnings, its lowest since October 2022 and 24% below its January 2026 peak; forward earnings had risen ~14% since June while the multiple shrank ~19%; the NDX premium over the S&P 500 was ~5%, the smallest since January 2017, against a ~20% 10-year average; over the prior month the NDX fell ~10% while the equal-weight S&P 500 rose ~5%. The page returned HTTP 403, so these figures come from the note's search-indexed text. INFERENCE: the NDX has fallen further since (27,002 on Nov 17 vs 27,990 on Nov 2), so if estimates held, the multiple is lower still.
findings.relevance: The drawdown is shrinking valuation multiples while earnings estimates rise, not earnings cuts. It is also narrow: equal-weight stocks rose while the NDX fell. Valuations are much less stretched than at the January peak, but only as reliable as AI-linked earnings.

findings.claim: FORECAST/OPINION: Goldman Sachs estimates, as reported by Fortune on Nov 17, 2026. AI investment has lifted S&P 500 earnings ~25% above trend, and AI capex drives ~half of 2026 EPS growth. Hyperscaler capex adds ~12pp to EPS growth in 2026 and ~9pp in 2027, then becomes a ~5pp drag in 2028. S&P 500 EPS growth ~30% in 2026 and ~11% in 2027 (18% excluding mega-cap tech 'other income'). Forward P/E is down 19% this year to ~18x. Year-end-2027 S&P 500 target: 8,700. Consensus (FactSet) has hyperscaler capex rising ~58% next year to ~$1.4T, then ~$1.54T in 2028. RELATED FACT: Amazon's Q3 2025 GAAP EPS included $9.5B of pre-tax gains on Anthropic investments, and Alphabet's Q3 2026 GAAP EPS included an $8.7B loss on equity securities (FactSet Earnings Insight, 2026-10-30). Mega-cap EPS now swings with marks on stakes in AI labs.
findings.relevance: This is the crux for a Nasdaq-100 trend strategy. The now-lower multiples rest on capex-driven earnings that Goldman expects to fade into a drag by 2028. If a hyperscaler announces a capex cut (52% of BofA survey respondents expect one within six months), it would hit both chip earnings and mega-cap valuations.

findings.claim: FACT: Nov 5, 2026 was the biggest one-day shock of the episode, two days after midterms in which Democrats won both chambers of Congress (Gray DC/Atlanta News First, 2026-11-04, https://www.atlantanewsfirst.com/2026/11/04/midterm-election-results-three-things-know/). Moves: Nasdaq-100 -6.3% (~$2.3T erased), Nasdaq Composite -5.5%, S&P 500 -4.3%, Dow -3.4% (more than 1,800 points), PHLX Semiconductor -12%, AMD -15%. The VIX jumped more than 65% to 27.45 intraday. Explanations reported: Nomura's Charlie McElligott (OPINION) said the main catalyst was hedge funds locking in profits before year-end, not fundamentals. Systematic and leveraged strategies were described as forced sellers, and retail sold stock on net at a pace not seen since 2020. There were also worries that the Democratic sweep could hit the AI data-centre buildout. NPR headlined it 'Fears of an AI crackdown after midterms spark $2 trillion rout in tech stocks' (2026-11-05, https://www.npr.org/2026/11/05/nx-s1-6031987/stock-markets-ai-midterm-elections; body not retrievable). Pressure resumed later: the Nasdaq fell 2.5% on Nov 16 (Fortune, 2026-11-17). On Nov 17 the S&P 500 fell for a 4th straight day to its lowest close since July 29, and the Nasdaq Composite touched its lowest since April intraday (CNBC live, updated 2026-11-18).
findings.relevance: Shows the gap risk in this regime: a single -6.3% NDX day is roughly -19% for a 3x daily-reset product, before costs. Days like this also feed the ~35% 20-day realised vol. It added a new political and regulatory driver (AI and data-centre policy under a Democratic Congress) that did not exist before Nov 3.

findings.claim: FACT: Nvidia is a top weight in both the NDX and the S&P 500. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president and director, effective immediately, on Nov 12, 2026, after reports of extramarital relationships, one of them reportedly with an executive of Singapore-based customer Megaspeed whom US officials reportedly linked to Chinese intelligence (denied). CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, and Harvey Jones became the first board chair. Shares were down more than 13% at the open on Nov 12 and closed -4.3% (CNBC live, 2026-11-12). By the Nov 16 close NVDA was ~35% below its October all-time high, about $2T of market value lost. Options implied a 7% earnings move, the largest since Feb 2025 (CNBC, 2026-11-17). Q3 FY27 results (Nov 17; quarter to Oct 25): revenue $115.8B (+103% y/y, +20% q/q) vs ~$109.1B consensus. Data Center revenue $107.6B (+110% y/y). GAAP gross margin 74.8%. Q4 guidance: $130B ±3%, including an extra week and assuming no China data-centre compute revenue, with gross margin guided down to 71-72%. $28.1B was returned to shareholders in Q3. The release refers to an independent board committee investigation and the CEO search. The stock rose ~4% after hours, and Nasdaq-100 futures were +0.6% at 2:41am ET on Nov 18 (CNBC live). findings.claim: FACT: BofA Global Fund Manager Survey (fielded Nov 6-12, released Nov 17). Managers cut tech by the most since June 2006: net overweight fell to 12% from 37%, per KuCoin's summary (https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/bank-of-america-survey-shows-fund-managers-cut-tech-exposure-at-fastest-pace-since-2006, 2026-11-17). Cash is 3.6% (BofA: 'uber-low'). 52% expect at least one AI hyperscaler to announce a capex cut within six months. Only 16% want companies to raise capex, the lowest since May 2020. 38% name hyperscaler bonds as the most likely source of a credit event, vs 30% for private credit. Per KuCoin, a record net 38% say companies are over-investing in AI, and long semiconductors is still the most crowded trade (39%, down from 82% in July). OPINION: BofA calls it the end of AI euphoria but 'not enough fear to buy'. Goldman Prime data (Hedgeweek, 2026-11-04, https://hedgeweek.com/news/hedge-funds-slash-leverage-at-fastest-pace-since-march-amid-october-losses): hedge-fund net leverage fell 4.2pp to 73.4% in October, the steepest drop in 7 months. ~$20B of tech was sold over two weeks, and selling from Oct 8-14 erased all net AI-equity buying since the start of 2025. In October, fundamental long/short funds returned -3.5% and systematic funds -3.6%, the first month since 2016 that both lost more than 3%.
findings.relevance: Institutions have cut tech risk a lot, but low cash and persistent semiconductor crowding mean sentiment is not capitulatory. That is consistent with high realised vol persisting and room for further de-leveraging if catalysts disappoint.

findings.claim: FACT: Mega-cap Q3 reports changed how the market judges AI spending: from 'capex = growth' to capex measured against free cash flow. That would be the first quarter since Q4 2022 in which the Mag-7 grew more slowly. Analysts also expect slower Mag-7 growth in Q4 (22.6% vs 30.8%). FactSet (2026-11-13): Mag-7 names that missed EPS (Alphabet, Amazon, Meta) averaged a -7.8% price reaction from two days before to two days after earnings, vs -0.2% for those that beat (Apple, Microsoft, Tesla). Alphabet: Q3 capex $51.4B vs $24B a year earlier, free cash flow -$9.1B, and a flagged 'significant increase' in 2027 capex (analysts ~$300B) (Fortune, 2026-10-28). Its shares fell ~13% on Oct 29, the worst day since the 2004 IPO, losing ~$475B, the 2nd-largest one-day loss for a US-listed company (Yahoo Finance, 2026-10-30). Q3 cash flow after capex: Alphabet -$9.1B, Meta -$1.2B, Oracle -$5.4B, Microsoft +$18.6B (TradingKey, 2026-11-15).

findings.claim: FACT: Regulation. On Nov 16, 2026, Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) issued an interim final rule. It requires licences for advanced AI-chip exports to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. Data centres must obtain licences before giving remote access to companies headquartered in China or other restricted destinations, with 90 days for existing customers. It formally rescinds the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule regulations, with a 60-day comment period. Commerce said the rule was 'written by and at the direction of' Treasury and the NSC. findings.relevance: Adds export-control and compliance risk to the semiconductor stocks that dominate NDX earnings growth. With a Democratic Congress after the midterms, policy is now an active driver of AI-stock volatility.

research.summary:
As of 2026-11-18, US data point to an overheating economy with an energy-driven inflation shock and a Fed that is raising rates, not to a recession. Q3 2026 GDP grew 3.4% annualized and the Q4 GDPNow nowcast is also 3.4%. October payrolls rose 165,000 and unemployment is 4.1%. The real-time Sahm-rule indicator is 0.00, against a recession trigger of 0.50. ISM manufacturing is 55.5 and services 54.5. Credit spreads remain tight: high-yield 3.34% and investment-grade 0.90% on Nov 16.

Published recession odds are low to moderate:
- NY Fed yield-curve model: 12.4% for the next 12 months.
- WSJ October survey of economists: 24%.
- Polymarket, recession by end-2026: about 2%.
- Goldman's 2027 outlook does not forecast a recession.

The main risks are:
- **Fed tightening:** it hiked to 3.75-4.00% in September, and a December hike is close to fully priced, with a 50 bp move floated.
- **Inflation from the Iran war:** September CPI was 3.7% y/y and core CPI is running +0.3% a month.
- **Squeezed consumers:** real disposable income fell 0.3% in September, the saving rate is 3.8% and sentiment is about 51.
- **Pockets of credit stress:** CCC-rated bonds and private credit.
- **Fiscal strain:** a $2.0T deficit (6.2% of GDP), funding that runs out Dec 11, and a debt-limit fight in 2027.

In the Nov 3 midterms Democrats won both chambers (Senate about 56-44 projected; House 254 D to 162 R with 19 races uncalled as of Nov 7). Markets read this as fiscal gridlock and as regulatory risk for AI. The post-election bond rally (10y at 4.88%) reversed within two weeks after strong jobs and inflation data.

My interpretation: the Nasdaq-100 drawdown looks driven by rates, valuations and AI rather than by recession. In this inflation-led environment, long Treasuries have not hedged equities. The web-search budget ran out near the end, so a few items could not be checked further.

findings.claim: The Fed is raising rates while the economy is strong. On Sep 16, 2026 it raised the target range 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00%. This was its first hike since July 2023, the vote was unanimous, and the Chair is Kevin Warsh. The September dot-plot median is 4.1% for both end-2026 and end-2027 (stockanalysis.com, 2026-09-17, https://stockanalysis.com/news/fed-raises-rates-by-quarter-point/). On Oct 28 the Fed held rates on a 10-2 vote. Gov. Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a hike. The statement says activity is 'expanding at a strong pace' and 'Inflation remains elevated'. After the Nov 6 jobs report, CME FedWatch put the odds of a 25 bp hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC at 76.8% (InvestmentNews, 2026-11-06). A Motley Fool article (2026-11-16) reports FedWatch at 100% as of Nov 12. The same article says Gov. Waller argued that a 50 bp hike 'should be considered' if October inflation came in hot, and that a 25 bp hike only 'would put our credibility at risk'.
findings.relevance: This is the main macro force behind the current regime. Higher policy rates and a 10-year yield around 5.1% compress valuations of long-duration tech stocks. Markets are reading strong data as hawkish. Key dates are the Dec 4 jobs report, the Dec 8-9 FOMC and the Dec 10 CPI. The exact December odds (100%, and 25 vs 50 bp) come from secondary sources, so confidence on those is medium.

findings.claim: Q3 2026 real GDP (advance estimate, released Oct 29) grew 3.4% annualized, up from 2.2% in Q2. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers grew 4.9%. Investment (inventories and equipment), consumer spending and federal spending all rose; net exports were a drag. The PCE price index rose 2.1% annualized in Q3 (5.0% in Q2), and core PCE 2.5% (3.3% in Q2). The Atlanta Fed GDPNow nowcast for Q4 2026 was 3.4% on Nov 17, after 3.5% on Nov 9 and 3.7% on Nov 2. Within it, consumption was 2.5% and investment 10.2% (https://www.atlantafed.org/research-and-data/data/gdpnow/current-and-past-gdpnow-commentaries, 2026-11-17). Treasury's TBAC statement (2026-11-02) puts Q3 business fixed investment at +12.7%.
findings.relevance: Hard activity data show no recession. My interpretation: the Nasdaq-100's 13.5% drawdown is happening alongside above-trend growth, which fits a rate and valuation shock better than an earnings or recession bear market. The second Q3 estimate is due Nov 25.

findings.claim: October payrolls rose 165,000 (BLS, released Nov 6), against a consensus of about 59,000 (InvestmentNews). August was revised to +186k and September to +60k, a combined +84k. Unemployment was 4.1% (4.2% in September) and participation 61.9%. Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% m/m and 3.1% y/y. Gains were led by professional and business services (+70k), health care (+42k), transportation and warehousing (+25k) and manufacturing (+19k). The real-time Sahm-rule indicator is 0.00 for October; the recession trigger is 0.50 (FRED SAHMREALTIME, updated 2026-11-06). Initial jobless claims were 200,000 in the week ended Nov 7, with a four-week average of about 195,000 (Fortune, 2026-11-16, https://fortune.com/2026/11/16/why-no-ai-layoff-wave-goldman-sachs-outlook-recession-jobs/).
findings.relevance: The labor market gives no recession signal. Its strength is the main reason markets expect more Fed hikes. The next jobs report is due Dec 4, and a shutdown after Dec 11 could delay it.

findings.claim: Inflation is speeding up again. Energy (the Iran war) leads, but the pressure is broadening. For September 2026: headline CPI 3.7% y/y, core CPI 2.6%, PCE 3.6% and core PCE 3.1%. Energy drove about 40% of the rise in CPI inflation, and energy CPI averaged +1.9% a month in Q3 (Treasury TBAC statement 2026-11-02; BEA 2026-10-29). October CPI (BLS, Nov 10): +0.4% m/m (September +0.6%). Core CPI rose 0.3% for a third straight month. Energy +0.7%, food +0.5%, shelter +0.3%, and gasoline +37.4% y/y. BLS did not publish the all-items 12-month change for October 2026, because October 2025 data were never collected during the 2025 shutdown. findings.claim:
Published recession-probability estimates (all are forecasts):
- **NY Fed yield-curve model:** 12.42% for the next 12 months (data through October, updated Nov 5; prior 12.76%).
- **Chauvet-Piger smoothed probability:** 0.40% (data through September) (EconomicGreenfield, 2026-11-09).
- **WSJ October survey** (71 economists, Oct 2-7): average 24%, range 1%-80% (25% in July). The same survey forecasts 2026 GDP at 2.42%, 2027 GDP at 2.14%, December 2026 unemployment at 4.19% and the December 2026 10-year yield at 5.10% (EconomicGreenfield, 2026-10-11).
- **Polymarket, 'US recession by end of 2026':** about 2% (page updated Nov 18).
- **Goldman Sachs 2027 outlook** (Nov 15-16): 2027 GDP 2.4% (consensus 2.2%), no recession forecast, two more Fed hikes, and cuts returning in late 2027.
- **Morgan Stanley:** cuts only in 2028 (CNBC 2026-11-16; Fortune 2026-11-16).
- **Moody's Analytics machine-learning model:** reported near 48% in spring and July 2026. This comes from secondary coverage, was not re-verified and may be stale.
findings.relevance: Consensus sees recession risk as a 2027 issue that depends on how far the Fed hikes, not as imminent. If these gauges rise, especially together with wider credit spreads, the regime would be shifting from a rates/valuation drawdown to a growth scare.

findings.claim:
Credit markets show no broad stress. The ICE BofA US high-yield option-adjusted spread was 3.34% on Nov 16 (3.20% Nov 12, 3.42% Nov 6, 3.48% Nov 5). The investment-grade spread was 0.90% (FRED, updated 2026-11-17). In early October high yield was at 315 bp, below the March 2026 peak of 346 bp (CNBC, 2026-10-09). Stress is concentrated in CCC-rated bonds, per Vanguard (2026-11-10):
- CCC spreads are about 1,000 bp, more than 500 bp above their 2026 lows.
- The CCC discount to the rest of high yield is the largest since COVID.
- Four issuers account for more than 30% of the CCC widening, and telecom/media are the weakest sectors.
- BB and B spreads are 'relatively contained'.
- The high-yield market yields 8.21%.
- S&P 500 EPS growth is 29%, with net debt/EBITDA about 2x, the lowest since 2014.

The St. Louis Fed Financial Stress Index was -0.49 for the week of Nov 6, up from -0.72 on Oct 9 (rising, but still below its zero average). The Chicago Fed NFCI was -0.462, looser than average (FRED, updated 2026-11-12).
findings.relevance: Credit has not confirmed the equity drawdown, a useful cross-check that the selloff is driven by valuations and rates. Signs of broader risk-off would be high-yield spreads moving clearly above the March 2026 peak of about 346 bp, or the St. Louis stress index turning positive.

findings.claim:
The Fed's Financial Stability Report (released Nov 13, data through Oct 28) found:
- The banking sector is 'sound and resilient'.
- Asset valuations are near the upper end of historical ranges.
- Hedge-fund leverage is the highest since 2013.
- Private-credit default rates have risen since May to the upper end of their historical range.
- Bank exposure to nonbank financial institutions exceeded $2.8T in Q2 2026, about a quarter of commitments.
- In its survey of contacts, about 90% cited elevated equity valuations and complex AI financing as risks; an AI-stock correction ranked second and higher long-term rates third (Reuters via Yahoo, 2026-11-14).

The October Senior Loan Officer Survey (released Nov 2) found tighter standards for C&I loans to small firms, for all CRE categories and for all queried loans to nondepository financial firms. C&I loan demand was weaker for firms of all sizes (https://www.federalreserve.gov/data/sloos/sloos-202610.htm). NY Fed Q3 household credit report: debt reached $19.1T (+$334B), and 5% of debt is in some stage of delinquency (+0.3 pp q/q). Mortgage transitions into serious delinquency worsened but remain historically low (ABA Banking Journal, 2026-11-10).
findings.relevance: There is no systemic bank stress. The weak spots are private credit and leveraged loans, CRE, small-business credit and lower-income households. These are slow-burning risks that would worsen if rates stay higher for longer, and they could amplify a downturn if one starts.

findings.claim: Consumers are squeezed by energy costs but still spending. September 2026 (BEA, Oct 29): personal income +0.2%, real disposable income -0.3% m/m, nominal spending +0.5% but real spending about 0.0%, and a saving rate of 3.8%. October retail sales (Census, released Nov 17) rose 0.2% m/m in nominal terms (September +0.8%), less than October CPI's +0.4%. Auto and furniture sales fell, and gas-station sales rose 1.5%. Opinions (UPI, 2026-11-17): Oxford Economics' Pearce says the consumer is 'bending, not breaking'; RBC's Reid says upper-income households are driving consumption. University of Michigan preliminary November sentiment was 51.0 (October 48.0), still about 10% below February. Year-ahead inflation expectations fell to 4.3% from 4.7%, and long-run expectations are 3.4%. 57% said high prices have eroded their living standards. Interviews ran Oct 20-Nov 2, before the election (https://www.sca.isr.umich.edu/).
findings.relevance: Consumers are the main soft spot. Falling real income and a low saving rate leave little buffer if energy prices rebound or hiring slows. October PCE is due Nov 25 and final November sentiment on Nov 20.

findings.claim: ISM Manufacturing PMI was 55.5 in October (September 54.5), the 10th straight month of expansion. Production was 59.0 (highest since November 2021), new orders 55.5, employment 52.4 and prices 75.2 (September 77.9). Customers' inventories were 41.6, which ISM calls 'too low'. Chair Susan Spence attributes the price pressure to steel and aluminum, tariffs, and 'petroleum-based products as a result of the Middle East conflict' (PR Newswire/ISM, Nov 2). ISM Services PMI was 54.5 (September 54.9), its 28th month of expansion. Employment was 51.4 (highest since February), prices 73 (second-highest since mid-2022), and new orders at a four-month low. Chair Steve Miller said 'more pricing pressure is on the way if oil and tariff cost impacts are not mitigated' (Bloomberg via Staffing Industry Analysts, 2026-11-04, https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/us-service-sector-grew-at-the-slowest-pace-in-3-months).
findings.relevance: Business surveys confirm expansion rather than recession. Price indexes above 70 confirm inflation pressure, which supports continued Fed tightening and keeps pressure on bond yields.

findings.claim: The Conference Board Leading Economic Index was flat at 99.6 in September 2026, after -0.1% in August. Its six-month change (March to September) was +0.6%, reversing the previous six-month decline. The Coincident index rose 0.3%. Consumer expectations were the largest drag. The yield spread (10-year minus fed funds) and manufacturing hours were the leading positive contributors. The Conference Board raised its GDP forecasts to 2.2% for 2026 and 2.0% for 2027. The October LEI is due Nov 19.
findings.relevance: Leading indicators show no recession signal. The positive yield-spread contribution matches the uninverted 10-year minus 3-month curve (about +1.0 pp) in the data you already have.

findings.claim: The FY2026 deficit (year ended Sep 30) was $2.0T. That is $218B more than FY2025 ($1.8T) and $140B above CBO's projection. Receipts were $5.4T (+3%) and outlays $7.4T (+6%). Net interest rose $115B (+11%). Customs duties fell $22B (-11%), as about $130B of $166B in eligible refunds were paid after the Supreme Court ruled the IEEPA tariffs illegal. The deficit was 6.2% of GDP (5.8% in FY2025), and debt held by the public is $32.4T, about 100% of GDP (American Action Forum on CBO data, 2026-10-08). Opinion: CRFB calls it 'the highest ever outside of a war or recession' (2026-10-08). Treasury's TBAC statement says the 10-year yield was 76 bp above its end-2025 level of 4.18% as of Oct 30, and that higher borrowing costs 'could worsen the federal debt trajectory' (2026-11-02).
findings.relevance: My interpretation: heavy Treasury issuance and rising interest costs keep a structural floor under long-term yields and the term premium. That is one reason long Treasuries have been an unreliable hedge in this cycle.

findings.claim: Government funding runs only to Dec 11, 2026, under the stopgap H.R. 6500 enacted in September. Before that came the record 43-day shutdown (Oct 1-Nov 12, 2025), a brief lapse in early February 2026, and a 76-day Homeland Security lapse (Feb 14-Apr 30, 2026) (Brookings, updated 2026-11-04). Kalshi odds of a shutdown rose to 45% from about 30% right after the election (Fortune, 2026-11-04, https://fortune.com/2026/11/04/wall-street-treasuries-yields-demand-budget-fiscal-gridlock/). The $41.1T debt limit could be hit as early as February 2027; Bank of America estimates about $557B of headroom. BofA forecasts the X-date in November 2027 but warns it could get 'uncomfortably close' by August 2027 (forecast). BMO warns of a long 2027 standoff, sovereign-downgrade risk and cash/repo volatility (opinion) (Fortune, 2026-11-09, https://fortune.com/2026/11/09/us-debt-limit-outlook-xdate-deadline-default-congress-summer-recess/).
findings.relevance: There is near-term event risk to the flow of economic data: the 2025 shutdown permanently erased October 2025 CPI data, and a December lapse could delay the jobs and CPI releases. A 2027 debt-limit fight could also disrupt T-bill and repo markets.

findings.claim: Democrats won both chambers on Nov 3. NBC projects a 56-44 Democratic Senate (+9 seats), including flips in Mississippi (Colom 49.4% vs Hyde-Smith 48.5%, 99% counted) and Alaska (Peltola 50.1% vs Sullivan 45.8%) (https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/senate-results). The AP count on Nov 7 had House Democrats at 254 and Republicans at 162, with 19 races uncalled (Express Tribune, https://tribune.com.pk/story/2639162/democrats-secure-additional-us-house-seats-as-more-midterm-races-called). Overnight, Asian AI stocks sold off and US futures fell sharply before recovering (Reuters). On Nov 4 the Dow rose more than 1,500 points (about 3%) to above 53,000, its best day since April 2025. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq each gained more than 1%, and Apple, Microsoft and Amazon rose 6% or more. AI-infrastructure names fell: CoreWeave and Nebius more than 7%, Nvidia 2%. Oil fell about 8% (CNBC). Treasuries rallied: the 10-year was at 4.884% (-6 bp), the 30-year at 5.273% and the 2-year at 4.573% (CNBC, https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/11/03/treasury-yields-fall-as-democrats-win-big-in-us-midterm-elections.html). The bond rally faded after the strong Nov 6 jobs report (10-year about 4.87%, 2-year 4.52%; InvestmentNews), and the data you already have show the 10-year at about 5.10% on Nov 17.
findings.relevance: The election produced a one-day relief rally and a short bond rally. Macro data (jobs and CPI leading to Fed hike pricing) quickly took over again, and the Nasdaq-100 still closed the week to Nov 6 about 4.9% lower (data you already have). Democratic control is high-confidence; exact seat counts are still provisional.

findings.claim:
How analysts read the result (all opinions):
- **Paul Donovan, UBS:** 'Fiscal gridlock seems the likely default.'
- **Jim Reid, Deutsche Bank:** divided government 'has generally made it harder for fiscal stimulus to be passed' (Fortune, Nov 4).
- **Charu Chanana, Saxo:** lower expectations of fiscal stimulus explain the softer dollar and the pressure on equities.
- **Andrew Lilley, Barrenjoey:** under a Republican sweep there was a roughly 5% tail risk of $5,000 payments to adults, which 'would have been a cataclysmic reaction from Treasuries'; that risk is now gone.
- **Tai Hui, J.P. Morgan Asset Management:** deficits may be more controlled, a debt-ceiling fight is expected next year, and Trump keeps his tariff and executive powers.
- **Jake Dollarhide, Longbow, and Nick Ferres, Vantage Point:** a Democratic Congress brings regulatory risk for AI, and Ferres adds crypto. Ferres notes the AI basket was more than 24% below its peak.
- **Tapas Strickland, Moomoo ANZ:** fears a slower AI data-center buildout in Texas and Georgia, which he puts at about a third of AI data-center spending.
- **Jesper Koll, Monex:** AI momentum was already turning negative regardless of the result, and markets may start to see more Fed independence (Reuters via Yahoo, Nov 4).
- **Counterpoint:** Wall Street expects Democrats to push for more Medicaid, housing and affordability spending when the debt limit has to be raised (Fortune, Nov 9).
findings.relevance: For a Nasdaq-100 strategy the political overhang is mostly sector-specific (AI regulation and the data-center buildout), not macro. The view that gridlock means fiscal restraint is contested, so the deficit and term-premium backdrop may not improve. The new Congress is not seated until January 2027.

research.summary:
In Oct-Nov 2026 one chain of cause and effect drives most cross-asset moves. The US-Israel war with Iran, running since late February 2026, and the disruption of the Strait of Hormuz caused an oil supply shock. That shock pushed inflation back up: US CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month in October, euro-area inflation reached 4.0%, and the Bank of England expects UK inflation near 5% by mid-2027. Central banks are now tightening together. The Fed raised rates to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 and markets price about 96% odds of another hike on Dec 9. The ECB's deposit rate is 2.50% after two hikes, the Bank of England moved to 4.00% on Nov 5, and the Bank of Japan holds at 1.25% while signalling further hikes.

This lifted the US 10-year inflation-adjusted (TIPS) yield to about 2.9%, close to its highest since 2008, and the 10-year nominal yield above 5%. The 10-year breakeven inflation rate is only about 2.3%, so most of the rise is in real yields. Three effects followed:
(a) The dollar index (DXY) reached a 19-20-month high near 103.5, but mostly because the euro fell. French fiscal stress (the French-German 10-year spread hit 130 bp on Oct 1) and Lagarde's early exit from the ECB on Feb 7, 2027 weighed on the euro. The yen is held near 160 by Japanese intervention with US backing, the yuan is at its strongest since 2022, and the Fed's broad dollar index is up only about 2% this year.
(b) Gold is about 30% or more below its Jan 28, 2026 record of about $5,590, trading around $3,770-3,850 at 13-month lows, even though central banks bought heavily in Q3 (321 tonnes).
(c) Treasuries and gold both fell alongside equities, so neither worked as a hedge. San Francisco Fed research describes this pattern as typical when supply shocks drive the economy.

Oil swung sharply. Brent rose 13.6% in October to about $113-118, then had its biggest weekly drop since 2020 in early November and now trades around $93-96. Gulf output has recovered to 97% of pre-war levels and the IEA now projects a Q4 surplus of 1.7 mb/d. Military exchanges since Nov 15 keep the risk of escalation live: an Iranian strike on a US base in Bahrain, mines reported in the Strait of Hormuz, and a US strike on Qeshm Island.

On trade, after the Supreme Court struck down tariffs imposed under emergency powers (IEEPA), US tariffs now rest on Section 301 (10-12.5% on 60 economies) and Section 232 (including 25% on semiconductors). China's US-China truce measures run to Jan 10, 2027. This week brings the APEC meetings in Shenzhen, including a Xi-Trump meeting and the first Xi-Trump-Putin meeting on Nov 19, and a new US Commerce Department rule (Nov 16) requiring licences for advanced AI-chip exports to Southeast Asia.

Side note: crypto exchange Binance lost a record $6.3bn to a hack on Oct 29, and bitcoin traded around $77k on Oct 30 (https://www.staradvertiser.com/2026/10/30/breaking-news/yen-gains-after-boj-holds-rates-dollar-slips/, 2026-10-30).

The shared web-search budget ran out before a final verification pass, so some items rest on a single source or on search snippets. These are flagged in the findings and unknowns.

findings.claim: Gold is falling because real yields are rising, not because official buyers are selling. On Nov 13 the US 10-year TIPS (inflation-adjusted) yield was about 2.87%, close to the highest for that maturity since Oct 2008. The 10-year nominal yield was 5.14% and the 10-year breakeven inflation rate only 2.26%, so the rise in yields is mostly real. That raises the cost of holding gold, which pays no income. Underlying demand data, from World Gold Council Q3 2026 figures released Nov 3: central banks bought 321t net (+42% y/y; 675t year to date), and physically backed ETFs took in 211t to reach record holdings. Bar and coin demand fell 19% to 268t and jewellery fell 17% to 313t, its weakest Q3 on record. In October (WGC, Nov 5), global gold ETFs added $2.7bn and holdings reached a record 4,275t, but North America was the only region with outflows (-$512mn). The WGC links US selling partly to investors raising cash during the tech-stock selloff over AI-spending concerns, and to money moving into Treasuries at multi-decade-high yields. Also: https://www.gold.org/news-and-events/press-releases/central-bank-buying-and-etf-inflows-support-gold-demand-q3/ (2026-11-03); https://tipswatch.com/2026/11/15/this-weeks-10-year-tips-auction-shows-a-lot-of-potential/ (2026-11-15).
findings.relevance: The user's risk-off sleeve holds gold. Gold is currently driven by the same factor that pressures long-duration Nasdaq stocks, rising real yields, so in this regime it has not offset equity risk. Strong official and non-US ETF buying has slowed the decline but not stopped it.

findings.claim: Gold's drawdown is deeper and older than a pullback from about $4,400. Spot gold set its record of about $5,590 intraday on Jan 28, 2026 (the LBMA PM benchmark peaked near $5,405). It fell 8.5% to $4,866.60 on Jan 30 when Trump nominated Kevin Warsh as Fed chair, and averaged $4,262 in Q3 (WGC). In mid-November it hit 13-month lows: down 3% to $3,867.96 on Nov 12 (lowest since Oct 2025), $3,833 on Nov 16, and about $3,774 on Nov 18 per one price page, roughly 32% below the record. According to BullionVault (London PM price), gold fell 15.1% in the 12 weeks to Nov 13, the fifth-steepest 12-week fall in 20 years, and was down in 10 of those 12 weeks. That followed a 15.8% 12-week drop earlier in the summer. Silver fell as much as 6% to $47.15 on Nov 16. Also: https://www.khaleejtimes.com/business/gold-drops-3-to-over-one-year-low-as-fading-middle-east-peace-hopes-fan-inflation-fears (Reuters, 2026-11-12); https://metalcharts.org/gold-all-time-high (price snapshot 2026-11-18; the record figure comes from this aggregator); https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/markets/2026/01/30/gold-plummets-and-dollar-strengthens-on-trumps-fed-chair-nomination/ (2026-01-31).
findings.relevance: This corrects the framing: gold has been in a drawdown of about 30% since Jan 28, 2026, not a pullback from $4,400. A 15% fall in 12 weeks is historically extreme, which matters for the volatility assumptions the strategy applies to its gold allocation.

findings.claim: Hedges are behaving differently in this regime. A San Francisco Fed Economic Letter (2026-21, Mertens and Wasserburger, Aug 10, 2026) measures the 5-year trailing monthly correlation between S&P 500 returns and the 10-year Treasury yield. It turned negative again in the early 2020s: stocks fall when yields rise, so Treasuries lose money alongside equities. The stock-oil correlation also changed sign. The authors explain this with negative oil supply shocks: higher oil raises inflation and bond yields while lowering activity and stock valuations. Their interpretation (opinion): a structural shift toward a supply-driven economy that 'may be the new normal for some time.' The letter gives no exact 2026 correlation values. Consistent with this, the US 10-year yield touched 5.33% on Oct 1, the highest since 2007 (FXStreet, 2026-10-02: https://www.fxstreet.com/analysis/the-us-dollar-index-just-hit-new-2026-highs-above-10220-this-chart-shows-the-runaway-move-202610021505), before equities sold off.
findings.relevance: This explains why the Treasuries-plus-gold risk-off leg lost money (TLT -2.9%, GLD -5.2% since Jul 24) while the dollar (UUP), managed futures (DBMF) and 3-month bills at about 4.1% held up. When inflation from a supply shock is the driver, bonds and gold carry the same real-rate risk as equities.

findings.claim: The dollar's Oct-Nov rally is mainly a repricing of US interest rates. DXY reached about 103.5-103.6 on Nov 17-18, its highest since April 2025, after gaining more than 1% in the week to Nov 13. Triggers: October CPI rose 0.4% m/m (September +0.6%) and core CPI 0.3%, beating forecasts for a third straight month. The 12-month rate could not be published because October 2025 prices were not collected during the government shutdown. Fed officials sounded hawkish: Waller backs a December hike regardless of the data, and Musalem said up to four hikes may be needed. The Fed already raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 (first hike since 2023, 12-0 vote) and held on Oct 28, with Cook and Hammack dissenting in favour of a hike. On Nov 18, CME FedWatch showed about 96% odds of a 25bp hike on Dec 9 (about 4% for 50bp). Futures imply about four more hikes by Sep 2027, and the 2-year Treasury yield is about 4.7%. Also: https://www.fxstreet.com/analysis/the-us-dollar-just-hit-a-19-month-high-and-the-fed-isnt-done-202611121829 (2026-11-12); https://federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm (2026-09-16).
findings.relevance: Expectations of further Fed hikes are the common driver behind the stronger dollar, Treasury yields above 5% and gold's fall. The Dec 9 FOMC meeting and the Dec 10 CPI release are the next scheduled events that could shift this regime.

findings.claim: The DXY rally is narrow and led by the euro, not broad dollar strength. The euro, 57.6% of DXY, has fallen about 5% against the dollar since late August. It broke below 1.11 for the first time since May 2025 and was nearing 1.10 on Nov 16, a 19-month low. An FXStreet analyst estimates the euro accounts for about 2.7 points of DXY's 3.4-point gain from the August low to Nov 6. By contrast, the Fed's 26-currency broad dollar index is up only about 2% this year (DXY about 4%) and is still 3.6% below its April-2025 tariff-announcement-day level. The dollar is down more than 4% this year against the yuan, and USD/JPY (about 159.5) has barely moved. Euro-specific drags: the French-German 10-year spread hit 130bp on Oct 1, the widest since 2012, around France's 2027 budget (5% of GDP deficit target). Lagarde announced on Oct 29 that she will leave the ECB on Feb 7, 2027, with no successor named, ahead of France's April 2027 presidential election. Also: https://www.fxstreet.com/news/the-euro-sells-off-hard-as-the-french-german-bond-gap-widens-202610012232 (2026-10-01); https://www.fxstreet.com/news/forex-today-markets-turn-cautious-to-start-week-us-dollar-holds-firm-202611160721 (2026-11-16); https://www.fxstreet.com/analysis/the-us-dollar-just-hit-a-19-month-high-and-the-fed-isnt-done-202611121829 (2026-11-12).
findings.relevance: DXY and UUP overstate how broadly the dollar is strengthening. The move is concentrated in the euro, driven by European fiscal and political risk plus the rate gap, while the yen is held back by intervention and the yuan is rising. Keep this in mind when reading the dollar as a risk-off signal.

findings.claim: Oil is the underlying shock. The US-Israel war with Iran began in late February 2026, the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed, and Brent went from about $61 at the start of 2026 ($72.48 on Feb 27) to well above $100. AP, via search snippets only, reported an intraday high of $126.41 on Apr 30; Majalla cites a $112.19 peak on Mar 20; the two conflict. Brent rose 13.6% in October: the December contract expired at $117.64 on Oct 30 and the January contract settled at $113.43. It then fell 13-16% in the week to Nov 6, its steepest weekly drop since March 2020 (the size differs by source and contract), on hopes of a mediated deal and recovering Gulf exports. On Nov 4, as AP projected Democrats would take both chambers of Congress, Brent fell 8.6% intraday to $94.70 and the 10-year yield dipped to 4.89%. In mid-November Brent traded at about $93-96: it settled at $95.82 on Nov 12 and was below $93 on Nov 17-18. Also: https://www.nationthailand.com/news/40072956 (2026-10-31); https://en.majalla.com/node/332465 (updated 2026-08-11); https://www.wect.com/2026/11/04/stock-futures-rise-after-democrats-take-control-congress/ (AP, 2026-11-04).
findings.relevance: Oil is the root cause of the inflation and rate shock that ended the Nasdaq-100 uptrend. Its direction is the biggest single swing factor for yields, the dollar and gold.

findings.claim:
Oil supply is recovering, but the war is not over. OPEC+ pumped 41.23 mb/d of crude in October, up 2.04 mb/d from September and 97% of the pre-war February level, helped by 'dark crossings' of Hormuz where tankers switch off tracking (Reuters, Nov 13). Iraq reached an understanding with the US to ship oil through a lane near Oman. US crude inventories rose 5.3m bbl in the latest week, and the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 279.5m bbl, the lowest since 1982. Escalation risk remains live:
- 35 vessels were hit in October, the highest monthly total of the war (UKMTO).
- Nov 12: Trump said the US no longer needs a deal with Iran.
- Nov 15: Iran struck a US helicopter base in Bahrain, its first attack on a Gulf state in weeks.
- Nov 16-17: Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said several tankers hit mines in the Strait (not independently verified).
- The US struck an Iranian missile site on Qeshm Island, and a third US aircraft carrier arrived.
- Yemen's Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, Yanbu and Riyadh.
- Ukrainian drones hit Russia's Ust-Luga port and Ryazan refinery.
Iran demands an end to the US naval blockade, sanctions relief and release of frozen assets before fully reopening Hormuz. VP Vance said the US will not let the conflict become a prolonged commitment. Also: https://gcaptain.com/world-oil-market-is-returning-to-surplus-as-gulf-exports-recover/ (2026-11-13); https://www.khaleejtimes.com/business/oil-falls-almost-5-as-trump-signals-restraint-on-iran (2026-11-09); https://www.nationthailand.com/news/world/40073442 (2026-11-13); https://www.nationthailand.com/news/40073162 (2026-11-06).
findings.relevance: Risk runs both ways. The physical oil market is loosening, which would eventually ease inflation and yields. Military escalation in the Gulf could send oil and yields sharply higher again, and that is the main source of sudden gap risk for leveraged positions.

Forecasts and opinions on oil and geopolitics (not facts):
- IEA Oil Market Report (Nov 13): Q4-2026 supply about 105 mb/d, 1.7 mb/d above demand (it had earlier forecast a deficit); 2026 world demand down 2.7 mb/d to 102.3 mb/d as high prices curb use; a surplus of about 3.8 mb/d in 2027.

Next scheduled catalyst (fact): the 21-member OPEC+ ministerial on Nov 29 sets 2027 quotas; the UAE left OPEC in May 2026. Also: https://www.nationthailand.com/news/40073162 (2026-11-06); https://www.staradvertiser.com/2026/11/01/breaking-news/opec-keeps-december-oil-output-targets-steady-as-iran-war-disrupt-flows/ (Reuters, 2026-11-01); https://www.wect.com/2026/11/04/stock-futures-rise-after-democrats-take-control-congress/ (2026-11-04).
findings.relevance: This sets out the range of scenarios for inflation and rates, from a 2027 glut to a $110-125 escalation spike. These are projections, not data. The OPEC+ meeting on Nov 29 is a dated catalyst.

findings.claim:
Tightening is global. That limits the dollar's interest-rate advantage and drains liquidity worldwide.
- ECB: held its deposit rate at 2.50% on Oct 29 after hikes in June and on Sep 10. It said energy prices 'have continued to rise' (an upside inflation risk) and that a larger, longer energy shock pushes inflation up and growth down. Euro-area flash inflation hit 4.0% in October, the highest since Sep 2023 (energy +20.8%, core 2.5%). FXStreet (Nov 11) reports traders expect a December ECB hike, and Chief Economist Lane said one would be prudent if the data hold.
- BoE: raised rates 25bp to 4.00% on Nov 5 (8-1 vote, Mann wanted 50bp), its first hike since Aug 2023. It projects UK CPI rising from 3.5% to about 5% by mid-2027.
- BoJ: held at 1.25% on Oct 30 but raised its inflation outlook and signalled hikes every few months.
- RBA: has raised rates five times.
Also: https://tradingeconomics.com/euro-area/inflation-cpi/news/598103 (2026-11-04); https://tradingeconomics.com/united-kingdom/interest-rate/news/598618 (2026-11-05); https://www.staradvertiser.com/2026/10/30/breaking-news/yen-gains-after-boj-holds-rates-dollar-slips/ (2026-10-30).
findings.relevance: With the Fed, ECB, BoE, BoJ and RBA all tightening, there is no easing elsewhere to cushion global liquidity. That is a headwind for high-multiple growth stocks and for gold, which pays no yield. It also limits how far the dollar can climb on rate differentials.

findings.claim: US-China trade and tech catalysts cluster this week. On Nov 9 China extended to Jan 10, 2027 its suspension of a 24% extra tariff on US goods (a 10% tariff stays), along with waivers on critical-mineral export controls, unreliable-entity measures and port fees. A $60bn reciprocal tariff-cut package from the September Washington summit is not finalised. China also noted US plans to use Section 301 to replace the invalidated IEEPA tariffs. Xi hosts APEC in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19, including a Xi-Trump meeting and the first Xi-Trump-Putin meeting (Nov 19); outcomes were not yet available. On Nov 16 the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim rule requiring licences for certain advanced AI chips and servers shipped to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, and curbing Chinese remote access to US chips through overseas data centres. Trading Economics reported (Nov 18) that Beijing warned of countermeasures. Rule details come from secondary coverage, not the Federal Register text. Also: https://tradingeconomics.com/china/currency/news/597939 (2026-11-04, updated 2026-11-16/18); https://chinaglobalsouth.com/2026/11/16/2026-apec-summit-shenzhen-china/ (2026-11-16); https://www.scmp.com/tech/article/3374639/us-tightens-ai-chip-export-curbs-close-chinas-overseas-data-centre-loophole (2026-11-16, not fetched).
findings.relevance: This bears directly on Nasdaq-100 semiconductor and AI names. The new export-licensing rule and the APEC meetings are near-term event risks, and the truce deadline is Jan 10, 2027.

findings.claim: The yen is a managed pressure point with explicit US involvement. After USD/JPY broke 160, Japan spent a record ¥11.73tn selling dollars in Apr-May 2026. With the yen near 164 per dollar, a 40-year low, the US Treasury and Japan jointly bought yen on Jul 31. The US sold euro reserves to do it, its first support for the yen in decades, and the yen rose to 155.20. Treasury Secretary Bessent said the US 'will not hesitate to participate in further joint intervention' and called the yen 'substantially undervalued.' Japan's 10-year JGB yield briefly hit 3.11% on Sep 25, a 30-year high. In mid-November USD/JPY was about 159.5 (Nov 16), back near the zone where Japan has intervened, and Japan's Q3 GDP shrank 0.1% annualised against an expected +0.3%. Also: https://www.cfr.org/articles/why-the-u-s-intervened-to-prop-up-japans-yen (2026-08-04); https://www.fxstreet.com/news/japanese-yen-gains-amid-intervention-watch-as-jgb-bond-yields-hit-30-year-highs-202609250630 (2026-09-25); https://www.fxstreet.com/analysis/why-the-us-dollars-rally-isnt-as-strong-as-it-looks-202611111707 (2026-11-11); https://www.fxstreet.com/news/forex-today-markets-turn-cautious-to-start-week-us-dollar-holds-firm-202611160721 (2026-11-16).
findings.relevance: Yen intervention, now with explicit US backing, can trigger sudden currency moves and unwinds of yen-funded carry trades that spill into global equities and Treasuries. It also caps how much the yen can add to dollar strength.

findings.claim: China's economy is running at two speeds, with exports riding the global AI hardware cycle. Q3 GDP grew 4.5% y/y (per search snippets, e.g. https://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2026/10/19/china039s-q3-gdp-growth-accelerates-to-45-beating-forecast, 2026-10-19). October exports rose 35.2% y/y to about $412bn: semiconductor exports +137.1%, autos +37.6%, exports to the US +32.9%. Imports rose 41.6%, partly because Gulf crude shipments recovered, and the Jan-Oct trade surplus reached $1.04tn. Domestic demand is weak: October retail sales +0.4% y/y, industrial output +4.8% (5.5% in September), fixed-asset investment -8.1% for Jan-Oct (People's Daily/NBS, 2026-11-16). The offshore yuan reached about 6.64 per dollar on Nov 2, its strongest since 2022 and up more than 4% this year. The PBOC slowed the rise by lifting banks' foreign-currency reserve requirement from 4% to 6% from Nov 15, while setting the Nov 18 daily fixing at 6.7118, the strongest since July 2022. Opinion: Moody's Dave Chia warns that an AI slowdown or correction could hit Chinese exports hard. Also: https://en.people.cn/n3/2026/1116/c90000-20519382.html (2026-11-16); https://tradingeconomics.com/china/currency/news/597478 (2026-11-03).
findings.relevance: China's export boom rests on the same AI hardware cycle that dominates the Nasdaq-100, so a turn in that cycle would show up in both. Weak Chinese domestic demand and a managed, strengthening yuan also shape global growth and the broad dollar trend.

findings.claim: The US tariff regime was rebuilt in 2026 on new legal grounds. The Supreme Court struck down tariffs imposed under emergency powers (IEEPA) on Feb 20, 2026. A 10% global surcharge under Section 122 filled the gap until it expired on July 24. On July 23 the President imposed Section 301 'forced labor' tariffs of 10% or 12.5% on 60 economies, with exemptions for USMCA-compliant goods and others. The June proposal set 10% for Canada, the EU, Mexico, Indonesia, Ecuador and Pakistan, and 12.5% for 54 others including China, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, the UK and India. Brazil faces 25% under a separate Section 301 action. Section 232 sector tariffs remain: steel, aluminium and copper 10-50%, autos 15-25%, semiconductors 25%, patented pharmaceuticals 10-100%, polysilicon 10-15% from Dec 4, 2026, and a timber increase on Jan 1, 2027. Section 338 imposes 50% on selected Canadian goods with no USMCA exemption. Customs has been refunding IEEPA duties: more than $20.6bn disbursed by end-May, per Barnes & Thornburg. Also: https://btlaw.com/en/insights/alerts/2026/tariffs-update-the-roller-coaster-ride-continues (2026-06-09); https://www.clearygottlieb.com/news-and-insights/publication-listing/trump-administration-imposes-new-section-301-tariffs-on-60-trading-partners (2026-08-03).
findings.relevance: Broad tariff headline risk is lower than in 2025, but sector duties hitting Nasdaq-100 constituents (25% on semiconductors, pharmaceuticals) and the Canada action persist. IEEPA refunds give importers a modest fiscal boost. Lawsuits and rate changes remain possible.

findings.claim:
Views on gold (opinions):
- Nicky Shiels of MKS Pamp (Nov 16): gold and silver are 'so clearly trading like a bear market', 'a tactical bear market inside a structural bull market'.
- Bruce Ikemizu of the Japan Bullion Market Association: there are 'plenty of reasons to sell gold' in the short term.
- Louise Street of the WGC (Nov 3): the outlook is 'finely balanced'; rising rates are a headwind, while geopolitical or financial stress could support gold.

research.summary:
Trend following had a strong 2026, but the gains came from bonds, oil and the dollar, not from equities. The SG CTA Index returned +15.7% in the nine months to end-Q3 by shorting Treasuries, holding crude bought in January before the Iran war, and staying long the dollar. Since early October those trends reversed during the Nasdaq correction, so trend did not hedge the equity sell-off this time. SG estimates as of 2026-11-18 put SG Trend at +11.62% YTD (November MTD -2.43%) and SG CTA at +11.54% (MTD -2.05%). Implied October for SG Trend was about -1.2% (derived). The user's risk-off sleeve has not protected in 2026. TLT is -5.2% YTD and GLD -11.1% YTD (-29% from its 2026-01-29 peak), and both were still in downtrends in mid-November. This fits IMF evidence that stocks and bonds have tended to fall together in stress since about 2020. Risk parity (RPAR) is -1.3% YTD and -10.6% from its February peak.

Leveraged Nasdaq ETFs show heavy volatility drag. YTD to 2026-11-17, TQQQ is -1.15% against QQQ +7.31% and QLD +5.19%. TQQQ is -40% below its June-2 peak and never regained it, even though QQQ made a new high on Oct 6. On 2026-11-05 the Nasdaq-100 fell 6.36% in one day, its worst since March 2020. Model estimates for that day include about $56bn of equity selling from leveraged-ETF rebalancing (Barclays) and about $61bn of potential vol-control selling (Nomura). Retail kept buying the dip: TQQQ took $3.5bn of inflows in October while losing 20.5%.

- **SEC:** the SEC tightened its stance on new products above 2x leverage: warning letters in Dec 2025, pushback in Mar 2026, a June 30 2026 request for comment on novel ETFs that includes heightened leverage, and a first Rule 18f-4 enforcement action in July 2026. Funds already operating in 2020, such as TQQQ, remain exempt from the 200% VaR limit. On 2026-10-02 the SEC approved listing of six 3x commodity and crypto ETPs, which are not yet trading.
- **Single-stock leveraged ETFs:** the first negative-NAV wipeout happened (LCDL, 2026-07-14), and 63 such funds closed by late August, against 3 in 2025.

  - Abolished the capital value tax on residents' foreign assets.
