findings.claim:
FACT: State Bank of Pakistan Foreign Exchange Manual, Chapter 20, para 13. The paragraph is footnoted to FE Circular No. 01 of 2024-07-11; the current PDF on sbp.org.pk was retrieved 2026-11-18.
- **Limit:** resident individuals may invest in shares of listed companies abroad under a general permission, through one designated Authorized Dealer branch, up to USD 25,000 per calendar year.
- **Concentration:** at most 1% of any single investee company.
- **Eligibility:** the funds must be legitimate and tax-paid, and the investor must be on the Active Taxpayer List.
- **Reporting:** a V-100 return is due within one month of investing.
- **Repatriation:** dividends and disinvestment proceeds, including capital gains, must be repatriated to Pakistan through banking channels and converted to PKR. They cannot be credited to a foreign-currency account.

No 2026 circular amending this was found; the 2026 SBP circulars located concerned non-residents' investment into Pakistan.
findings.source_date: FE Circular No. 01 dated 2024-07-11 (PDF retrieved 2026-11-18; no 2026 amendment found)
findings.relevance: If a live IBKR account is funded from Pakistan, the USD 25k/year cap and the mandatory repatriation of gains are binding limits on scaling and compounding. Two points are unresolved (see unknowns): whether ETF units count as listed-company shares, and whether funds already held in the UAE account fall under this regime.

findings.claim:
FACT: Pakistan's Finance Act 2026 was enacted 2026-06-27 and took effect 2026-07-01 (KPMG Taseer Hadi brief, July 2026). Relevant changes:
- (a) The Capital Value Tax on foreign assets of resident individuals was abolished (PwC tax summary, last reviewed 2026-08-24, https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/pakistan/individual). Before abolition it was reported as 1% where foreign assets exceeded Rs100m; that rate and threshold come from secondary summaries and are not verified.
- (b) Advance tax on amounts remitted abroad by credit, debit or prepaid card (s.236Y) was cut from 5% to 0.5%.
- (c) Tax rates for non-salaried individuals are unchanged, with a top rate of 45% above Rs5.6m.
- (d) For persons not on the Active Taxpayers' List, the s.37A capital-gains rate is increased by 100%.
- (e) Banks and e-money institutions must upload deposit and withdrawal data to a Central Data Hub for account holders whose aggregate deposits or withdrawals exceed Rs100m, for algorithmic cross-matching. SBP may also run a central repository of banking data on high-risk persons.

NEITHER source says how gains on foreign-listed ETFs are taxed. PwC says gains on movable capital assets other than exchange-traded securities are taxed at slab rates, and it describes the 15% s.37A rate for listed securities without saying whether foreign listings qualify.
findings.relevance: Removing the CVT lowers the annual carrying cost of a large offshore portfolio. The non-filer penalty and bank-data matching raise the cost of not declaring foreign assets and income. The key open number for after-tax backtests is whether foreign ETF gains are taxed at 15% or at slab rates up to 45%.

findings.claim:
FACT:
- **Pakistan residency:** an individual is resident with 183 or more days in the tax year. A Pakistani citizen is also resident if not present in any other country for more than 182 days, or if not a resident taxpayer of any other country (PwC, last reviewed 2026-08-24, https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/pakistan/individual/residence).
- **UAE residency:** individual tests are unchanged. They are (i) primary residence plus centre of financial and personal interests in the UAE; (ii) 183+ days in a 12-month period; or (iii) 90-182 days plus proof of UAE employment or business, or of a permanent place of residence. These follow the FTA guide of 2024-10-18 (KPMG UAE summary, https://kpmg.com/ae/en/home/insights/2024/10/uae-tax-resident-and-tax-residency-certificate-guide.html). No 2026 amendment was found.
- **CRS:** the UAE Ministry of Finance's CRS Participating Jurisdictions list (June 2026 version, modified 2026-06-23) includes Pakistan as entry 91.
- **Crypto reporting:** the UAE ratified the crypto-asset reporting agreement (CARF) by Federal Decree No. 60 of 2026. It takes effect 2027-01-01, with first exchanges in 2028 (UAE MoF page updated 2026-11-18, https://mof.gov.ae/en/public-finance/international-relations/automatic-exchange-of-information-aeoi-crypto-asset-reporting-framework-carf/).
findings.source_date: UAE MoF list 2026-06-23; PwC 2026-08-24; FTA guide 2024-10-18; MoF CARF page 2026-11-18
findings.relevance: A UAE bank account does not create UAE tax residency. A Pakistan-resident citizen is taxable in Pakistan on worldwide income, and UAE account data sits inside the automatic-exchange framework. Whether the Pakistan-UAE bilateral exchange is actually activated is unconfirmed. Planning should assume UAE and IBKR balances are visible to Pakistan's tax authority (FBR).

findings.claim:
FACT: US leveraged-ETF regulation tightened for new products in 2026 but did not touch existing 3x index funds.
- **Background:** Rule 18f-4 (adopted 2020-10-28) effectively limits new leveraged and inverse funds to 200% of index returns. It exempts leveraged and inverse funds already in operation from the VaR requirement (SEC press release 2020-269 fact sheet, https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2020-269). That is why pre-2020 3x funds such as TQQQ still trade.
- **Dec 2025 and Mar 2026:** SEC staff halted review of filings above 2x and sent warning letters to nine issuers in Dec 2025, then pushed back on 5x plans in March 2026 (Decrypt, 2026-10-05; Bloomberg headline 2026-03-03).
- **2026-06-30:** the SEC issued a Request for Comment on 'Novel ETFs' (Release 33-11426) covering heightened leverage and single-stock strategies; comments closed 2026-08-31.
- **2026-07-27:** the first enforcement action under Rule 18f-4: an ETF exceeded its VaR leverage limits, with a $400k penalty (Davis Polk, Sept 2026).
- **2026-10-02:** the SEC approved a Cboe BZX rule change to list six 3x Volatility Shares products on bitcoin, ether, gold, silver, crude and natural-gas futures. They cannot trade until their registrations go effective (Decrypt, 2026-10-05, https://decrypt.co/380108/sec-clears-3x-leveraged-bitcoin-ethereum-funds).

No final 2026 rule restricting existing leveraged ETFs was found.
findings.relevance: TQQQ and QLD remain available. The main product-availability risk is a future rule following the Novel-ETF request for comment, whose outcome is unknown. A 3x gold product, if launched, would add a new instrument for an off-leg sleeve, with the same daily-reset decay.

findings.claim:
FACT: Leveraged single-stock ETFs had their first wipe-out and a closure wave in 2026.
- **Wipe-out:** GraniteShares' 2x Long LCID Daily ETF (LCDL) closed out its whole Lucid position on 2026-07-14 at a loss that turned its NAV negative, and began delisting (GraniteShares notice, 2026-07-14).
- **Closures:** Reuters (2026-08-25, via https://wsau.com/?p=1009860), citing Morningstar, reported 63 US leveraged single-stock funds closed so far in 2026, against 3 in 2025.
- **Launches:** a record 244 leveraged ETFs launched by mid-August, against 229 in all of 2025.
- **Fund size:** the average leveraged ETF shrank from $272.2m at end-2024 to $63.3m, and half have under $7m.
findings.relevance: This shows the terminal-loss and forced-liquidation mechanics of daily-reset leverage, and the closure risk in small funds. TQQQ (index-based, about $37bn of assets) is far from these risks, but small UCITS or ETP leveraged trackers are not. Prefer large, liquid products and model forced liquidation on extreme days.

findings.claim: FACT: Risk parity has struggled in 2026. RPAR's total return is -1.29% YTD to 2026-11-17 and it is -10.63% below its 2026-02-27 high. RESEARCH ASSESSMENT: the IMF blog of 2026-02-18 argues that levered hedge-fund and risk-parity strategies built on the old negative stock-bond correlation now move increasingly with Treasury returns. That raises their exposure to forced deleveraging.
findings.relevance: This corroborates F1: balancing with bonds and gold has not diversified equity risk in 2026. A leveraged equity strategy whose defensive sleeve is bonds plus gold shares this exposure.

findings.claim:
FACT:
- **PRIIPs:** under IBKR's PRIIPs pages, a KID must be available to EEA and UK retail investors before they buy a PRIIP, which includes ETFs. Many US ETF issuers do not produce KIDs, so those clients are blocked from such US ETFs and are pointed to UCITS equivalents, CFDs or professional status. Source: IBKR knowledge base (undated); the content was seen via search results because IBKR domains could not be fetched directly in this session.

No evidence was found that either regime applies to a Pakistan-resident client.

The existing UCITS-above-$60k plan therefore rests on US estate-tax and withholding considerations (not re-verified here), not on KID rules. If the account were ever moved to an EU or UK IBKR entity, US leveraged ETFs could become unavailable.

brief.one_paragraph: FACTS: On Nov 17 the Nasdaq-100 closed at 27,002. That is 13.5% below its Oct 6 record, and the index has been below its 100-day EMA since about Oct 16. 20-day realised volatility is ~35% and the VIX is ~25.5. The fall came in shocks centred on AI mega-caps: -5.5% in the week to Oct 16, then -6.36% on Nov 5, the worst day since March 2020 (TQQQ -18.9%), two days after Democrats won both chambers. Company and policy news added to it: Alphabet's negative cash flow after capex, Nvidia's CEO resignation, and a new AI-chip export rule. The macro backdrop is inflationary tightening, not recession. INTERPRETATION (opinion): this looks like a 2022-style inflation and real-rate regime, with 2018-style tightening-correction dynamics and a 2000-style AI-capex-bust tail. It puts pressure on the system's bond/gold risk-off holdings and on its slow re-entry after a sharp rebound. The main scheduled catalysts are October PCE (Nov 25), the FOMC (Dec 8-9) and November CPI (Dec 10).
brief.regime_read:
INTERPRETATION (opinion, not a forecast): an inflation and real-rate shock combined with a sell-off in AI leaders, while the economy is still expanding. On current data this is a policy and valuation correction, not a recession or credit bear market.

Facts behind this read:
- The Fed is raising rates into 3.4% GDP growth, 4.1% unemployment and core CPI of +0.3% a month.
- The 10-year real yield (~2.9%) is near its highest since 2008, while breakeven inflation is only ~2.2-2.3%. Tighter real conditions, not fear about long-term inflation, are compressing valuations of long-duration growth stocks.
- Earnings are still rising while multiples fall: S&P Q3 EPS +31.9%, forward EPS +3.3% since Sep 30, and S&P tech's forward P/E (17.1) is now below the market's (17.9).
- Credit is calm: HY OAS 3.34%, IG 0.90%.
- The Sahm indicator is 0.00 and the 10y-3m curve is not inverted (NY Fed recession model 12.4%).

Closest analogs (opinion):
- 2022 for the macro mechanics: supply-shock inflation, Fed hikes, Treasuries an unreliable hedge, a firm dollar, gold pressured by real yields.
- Q4 2018 for the market shape: a tech correction driven by tightening, with earnings and credit intact, that reversed sharply once the rate path softened.
- Tail analog, 2000-02: a capex-financed tech boom unwinding. This is the one period in the cited backtest where buying after big weekly drops failed (0 of 18). It stays live because several hyperscalers have negative cash flow after capex, 52% of surveyed fund managers expect a capex cut, and consensus EPS growth falls to +3% by Q2 2027. Tech's ~17x forward multiple makes it a weaker match so far.

What the system's rules currently see (facts):
- Trend: off. NDX has been below its 100-day EMA since about Oct 16.
- Volatility: high. 20-day realised vol ~35%; VIX ~25.5 against ~15 in Aug-Sep.
- Choppiness: high. Three 10%+ drawdowns have started in 2026.
- Yield-curve overlay: not triggered. No 10y-3m inversion in the last 12 months.
- Bond hedge: intermittent.
- Gold: in a downtrend, ~32% below its January record.

What would change the read (opinion):
- Toward a growth scare: HY OAS clearly above its 2026 high (3.48%), a positive St. Louis Fed stress index and weakening payrolls. In that regime Treasuries have historically hedged better.
- Toward a 2018-style sharp rebound: a decisive fall in real yields after the Dec 8-10 catalysts.

key_facts.topic: Treasuries as a haven in November

November refunding $125bn: 3y $58bn, 10y $42bn, 30y $25bn. Providing significant computing power to companies headquartered in China-group (D:5) countries or Macau needs a licence; existing providers get 90 days. The rule formally rescinds the AI Diffusion Rule. BIS said Treasury and the NSC directed the rule. Beijing warned of countermeasures (Trading Economics).

Eurasia Group puts renewed US strikes at 60%, a prolonged standoff at 30% and a deal at 10%; escalation could lift Brent to $110-125. OPEC+ ministers meet Nov 29 to set 2027 quotas; the UAE left OPEC in May 2026.

October: global gold ETFs took in $2.7bn, reaching record holdings of 4,275t; North America was the only region with outflows (-$512mn). Xi meets Trump, and Trump and Putin, at APEC in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19. A Pakistan-qualified accountant or tax adviser, ideally one who handles Pakistan-UAE cross-border cases, must confirm every item below before any action. Open questions are listed under unverified: the tax rate on foreign ETF gains, the scope of the SBP rule, whether Pakistan-UAE CRS exchange is active, and the US estate-tax threshold.

State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) rule: Foreign Exchange Manual, Chapter 20, para 13, under FE Circular No. 01 of Jul 11, 2024. The current PDF was retrieved Nov 18, 2026, and no 2026 amendment was found.
- Resident individuals may invest in shares of listed companies abroad through one designated bank branch.
- Limits: up to USD 25,000 per calendar year, and at most 1% of any one company.
- The funds must be legitimate and tax-paid, and the investor must be on the Active Taxpayers' List (and financially sound, with a clean loan record).
- A V-100 return is due within one month.
- Dividends and sale proceeds, including capital gains, must be brought back to Pakistan through banking channels and converted to PKR; they may not be credited to a foreign-currency account.
The text does not say whether money already held abroad (for example in a UAE account) or ETF units are covered. That bears directly on the earlier working assumption that funding IBKR from the UAE account sidesteps this regime, which no source found confirms. Source: https://www.sbp.org.pk/assets/document/Chapter-20-foreign-exchange-manual.pdf

Pakistan Finance Act 2026 (enacted Jun 27, effective Jul 1, 2026; KPMG brief):
- Advance tax on card-based payments abroad (s.236Y) cut from 5% to 0.5% for active taxpayers (1% for others).
- Income tax slabs for non-salaried individuals unchanged; top rate 45% above Rs5.6m.
- The s.37A capital-gains rate is doubled for anyone not on the Active Taxpayers' List.
- Banks must upload deposit and withdrawal data for account holders above Rs100m in aggregate to a Central Data Hub for automated cross-matching; SBP may keep a central repository on high-risk persons.
- PwC (reviewed Aug 24, 2026) also lists the abolition of the capital value tax on residents' foreign assets; the KPMG brief does not mention it.
Sources: https://assets.kpmg.com/content/dam/kpmgsites/pk/pdf/2026/07/A%20Brief%20of%20Finance%20Act%202026.pdf.coredownload.inline.pdf ; https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/pakistan/individual

Capital gains: PwC (reviewed Aug 24, 2026) says gains on movable assets other than exchange-traded securities are taxed at normal slab rates, and that the 15% s.37A rate applies to listed securities held by filers on the Active Taxpayers' List. It does not say whether foreign-listed ETFs qualify for 15%. A weekly-rebalanced strategy realises gains often, so whether the rate is 15% or up to 45% changes after-tax results materially. An accountant must determine which applies. Source: https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/pakistan/individual

Tax residency:
- Pakistan (PwC): resident with 183+ days in the tax year. A Pakistani citizen is also resident if not present in any other country for more than 182 days, or if not a resident taxpayer of any other country.
- UAE (Federal Tax Authority guide of October 2024, via KPMG; no 2026 change found): resident if the primary residence and centre of financial and personal interests are in the UAE; or 183+ days in 12 months; or 90-182 days plus UAE employment or business, or a permanent UAE residence.
- Holding a UAE bank account is not one of these tests (inference).
Sources: https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/pakistan/individual/residence ; https://kpmg.com/ae/en/home/insights/2024/10/uae-tax-resident-and-tax-residency-certificate-guide.html

Information exchange: the UAE Ministry of Finance's list of jurisdictions taking part in automatic exchange of account information (CRS; Jun 23, 2026) includes Pakistan. Whether the Pakistan-UAE exchange is actually active is unverified. The UAE ratified the crypto-asset reporting framework (CARF) by Federal Decree No. 60 of 2026, effective Jan 1, 2027, with first exchanges in 2028. Planning should assume UAE bank and broker balances can become visible to Pakistan's tax authority, the FBR (inference). Sources: https://mof.gov.ae/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/CRS_List-of-Participating-Jurisdictions-23-June-2026.pdf ; https://mof.gov.ae/en/public-finance/international-relations/automatic-exchange-of-information-aeoi-crypto-asset-reporting-framework-carf/

Product availability: SEC Rule 18f-4 limits new leveraged funds to 200% of index returns but exempts funds already operating in 2020, such as TQQQ. 2x funds such as QLD sit within the 200% limit. The SEC's Jun 30, 2026 request for comment on novel ETFs, including heightened leverage (comments closed Aug 31), has no announced outcome, so future rules are a risk to product availability. Small leveraged products also carry closure and total-loss risk: 63 leveraged single-stock funds closed in 2026, and LCDL's net asset value turned negative on Jul 14. Sources: https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2020-269 ; https://www.davispolk.com/insights/client-update/investment-management-funds-regulatory-update-september-2026

EU/UK retail rules: EEA retail investors need a PRIIPs KID (key information document) to buy funds, and the UK's Consumer Composite Investments regime (FCA PS25/20) replaced UK PRIIPs KIDs from Apr 6, 2026, with full go-live on Jun 8, 2027. These could restrict access to US-listed ETFs only if the account were held as an EEA or UK retail client. No evidence was found that either applies to a Pakistan-resident client.
